title: What If Humans Could Breathe Underwater? Water Holds 30 Times Less Oxygen

scenes.text: What if you could breathe underwater? Gills wouldn't be enough. Water is the problem.
Air is about 21 percent oxygen. Water holds roughly thirty times less, so you'd have to move far more of it.
A person at rest would need to pass dozens of litres of water across their gills every minute.
Gills also need a huge thin surface, and being warm-blooded means burning oxygen faster than most fish.
In cold water you'd lose heat to the sea about twenty-five times faster than in air.
So the ocean would open up to you, and you'd spend most of the day just breathing.

description:
Water holds roughly thirty times less dissolved oxygen than air, so gills would have to push dozens of litres past you every minute.
Cold water would also pull heat from your body far faster than air.
